deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes Euler's table (begun on earlier pages of E283). For every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) below 2000 the table gives two things. First, a representation p = x² + y². Second, the residue class a ≡ ±r (mod p) for which p divides a² + 1. Here r is the root of −1 mod p lying in (0, p/2); it can be got as r ≡ x·y⁻¹ (mod p) from the two-square decomposition.

This page covers p = 1697 to 1997. The closing paragraph says the table contains all primes of the form 4n+1 below 2000. With it one can find every number a for which some prime of the table divides a² + 1.

The next page uses this as a sieve. List a = 1 to 2000. Attach 2 to the odd a, attach p to every a ≡ ±r_p (mod p) with a > p, and so on. This yields all prime divisors of a² + 1 that are smaller than a. Divisors larger than a then follow automatically. The purpose of the whole memoir ('De numeris primis valde magnis') is to find large primes of the form a² + 1, and hence large primes in general, by this sieve.

Modern view: tabulating square roots of −1 modulo p, then running a sieve along the polynomial values a² + 1.
errors: The decomposition for 1861 as it appears (read as 30² + 21² = 1341) is wrong; the correct value is 1861 = 30² + 31². This is either a printing defect or an OCR/print misreading; the root a = 61 is correct (61² + 1 = 2·1861).
I verified all other entries on this page: every a² + 1 is divisible by its p, and every two-square decomposition is correct. The list of primes ≡ 1 (mod 4) between 1697 and 1997 is complete.
Not on this page: the previous page's '1489 … a = 1389m ± 225' carries a misprinted modulus (1389 for 1489).

ideas.what: Table of the roots of a² ≡ −1 (mod p) for all primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4) below 2000, paired with the representation p = x² + y²
ideas.modern_name: Square roots of −1 modulo p; link to Fermat's two-square theorem (r ≡ x/y mod p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (two-square theorem proofs in the 1740s–50s); later large tables by Cunningham and Gauss-era tabulators
ideas.where_published: E283 itself (Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 9, 1764); related material in Euler's two-square papers (E228, E241)

ideas.what: Sieve along a² + 1 to obtain all prime divisors of a² + 1 below a, for a ≤ 2000
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial (quadratic) sieve / factor tables of n² + 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E283; later extended by Cunningham (Quadratic Partitions, 1904) and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is a computational table that is correct apart from one decomposition misprint. It belongs to a well-known Euler paper on primes of the form a² + 1; nothing on the page is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: 1861 = 30² + 21² should read 1861 = 30² + 31². The print appears to show '21' (likely a print defect or misprint); 31 is the arithmetically correct value.
